duration.$description:
Every value here was measured on a Phase 5 prototype rather than chosen, and the filmstrip run that produced it is named per token (`pnpm filmstrip`, docs/adr/tech/0037). Phase 5's design record is docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-01-phase-5-modernization-design.md.

These are consumed as custom properties in authored CSS, not as Tailwind utilities: Tailwind v4 has no `--duration-*` theme namespace, and the surface these were derived for — `::view-transition-group/old/new` — is document-level and unreachable from a utility class in the first place.

Deliberately small. A duration nobody measured is drift wearing a token's costume; add one when a prototype produces it, not in anticipation.

color.$description: Hover and focus colour changes — rule 1's carve-out, the only property that may animate on hover. Taken from the panel prototype's edit affordance (.13s), the one place the value was tuned against a pointer rather than guessed.

strike.$description: The subtask strike-through drawing across the label, and the label's colour shift beneath it. Long enough to read as a line being drawn rather than a state flipping; measured on task-open-v13 onward as `.22s`.

swap.$description: The box interpolation when the panel swaps from one task to another — `::view-transition-group`. Raised from 250ms after a filmstrip showed the whole transition completing in ~250ms and still reading as a cut; at 420ms the box travel is legible. Note this animates the BOX, never the text: see `text-out`/`text-in`.

text-out.$description: A swapped slot's outgoing text fading away. Overlaps `text-in` by 60ms so the slot is never empty — butting them end to end left the panel blank from +105ms to +190ms, which reads as fade-out-hole-fade-in rather than a swap.

text-in.$description: A swapped slot's incoming text arriving, starting at `text-in-delay`. Only applied to slots whose content actually differs; an unchanged slot keeps the UA's own complementary cross-fade, which is invisible where the pixels agree (measured 8.74 max wash with a custom curve against 1.11 with the default).

text-in-delay.$description: How long the incoming text waits before it begins, so old and new overlap by `text-out` minus this value. The overlap is what removes the blank frame; the offset in position is what keeps two different strings from double-inking while both are visible.

ease.$description: Curve choice is per-property, not per-phase — the single most expensive lesson of the Phase 5 motion work. Applying the phase curve to an opacity fade produced a blank frame; applying `linear` to a box morph produced no sense of weight. Pick by what is being animated.

standard.$description: Position and size — the box morph, the panel slide, anything travelling. Heavily front-loaded, which is what gives motion its sense of arriving rather than drifting.

fade.$description: Opacity, always, and `standard` never. `standard` is front-loaded enough that an opacity fade on it reaches ~0 in the first third of its duration, leaving a blank frame between the outgoing and incoming text — a flash, which reads worse than either a fade or a cut. Authored as the linear bezier rather than the `linear` keyword so it survives the DTCG `cubicBezier` type like its sibling.
